96

 How to make sure you get a good deal when buying or selling an accounting practice

 Watch a Lawyer Change Her Mind!
Hi Everyone,
I’m Sara Sharp, and I help people buy and sell accounting firms. After years of helping people with these deals, I've actually learned a new angle on one of the oldest terms out there: exclusivity. 
My Old Way of Thinking: Exclusivity isn't Enforceable So Who Cares
Historically I've noticed people don't even try to enforce an exclusivity provision because the dollar amount of damages is too low to justify hiring lawyer to fight it out (at least in these sub $5M deals).
The New Thought: Exclusivity is Can Be Pretty Powerful
You've heard me talk about the narrow sales window in these deals-spoiler it's SHORT. Basically a couple of months in the summer between tax seasons. By being exclusive for a short period of time, you can motivate people to push through diligence as fast as possible. 
What if You Combine it With a Good Faith Deposit?
Imagine you're a seller and you stop hearing from your buyer very often. Maybe they've lost the enthusiasm for the deal or they have a few under LOI and they're waiting to see how to allocate capital before they decide which deals to actually go through. What motivation do they have to cut you loose? 
Using Deposit + Exclusivity to = Efficiency
As you know, I hammer the drum of efficiency in small business deals. You're running a business, you don't have time to waste. Plus the only person who wins in an efficient deal process is the lawyer (tongue firmly in cheek). 
The Point of the Good Faith Deposit
Let's say the buyer submits a $15,000 good faith deposit tied to the seller agreeing to be exclusive for 60 days. 
So...
As the deal is waning in day 30, you suddenly have a motivation to let the other side know you're calling it so you can get your money back. Even more nuanced, the buyer has the sudden and significant motivation to admit it to themselves. This serves efficiency and frees both parties up to pursue a deal that'll actually close. GASP. So let me know, did I change your mind about the usefulness of these terms? Even just a little bit?
Thank you for being part of this journey. Have a wonderful weekend, and don’t forget to enjoy the little things.
Best,
Sara Sharp 
Deal Attorney
Partner, SK&S Law Group
P.S. If you have any questions about your next acquisition or sale, feel free to reach out for a consult call. I’m here to help you make your next deal a great one.
